preserved_assertions: Relocated fixtures retain their prior assertions; no snapshot auto-accept or unique assertion removal.

execution.quick: All behavioral scenarios once; sanitizer variants where supported.
execution.full: Same scenarios plus relevant optimization, ABI, role, kernel and supported-core checks.
execution.outputs: Use a fresh evidence directory; existing evidence is never overwritten.

gaps: Physical USB/BLE/split delivery, timing, power and retention require matching production-board evidence.
native_verification: tests/native_verifier.py: actual exit, registered test completion, raw ordered logs, unchanged snapshots, identical binary repeated three times.

custom_settings_dependency.required_contract: Same-slot keyspace rename, payload/storage identity and existing memory/persist lifecycle; both production import and isolated tests select this exact dependency. The selected registry also serializes mutations and retains notification targets through dispatch.
custom_settings_dependency.regression: Previous cormoran c6a7fef dependency lacks rename and fails enabled ARM/native links. Existing lifecycle fixtures retain same-slot rename assertions.
custom_settings_dependency.publication: The selected exact commit is published at the declared fork URL; prepare and verify that revision explicitly in the isolated container workspace.
custom_settings_dependency.selected_prerequisite: The selected c4071b095c3007d1deb055c609603ca9b5897d14 commit includes copy_public_key and encode-time local notification authorization. Production and isolated-test manifests pin that same implementation; a different working override remains a separate source snapshot requiring explicit identity and review.

timeout_width.contract: Full uint32 milliseconds, exact ceiling and configured kernel tick ABI; independent wide oracle and identified math/width controls

web_session.contract: Session retirement, latest selection, independent busy ownership, cleared deadlines and recoverable validated edits; body/JSON draft ownership survives rename/refresh and older read/save completions; name, next-creation-name and global tap drafts independently survive metadata reads and older mutation completions; full writes clear then append final prefixes without intermediate capacity inflation; uint32 overflow rejection preserves valid decoder inputs.
web_session.controls: Failing original editor/decoder; existing fractional-tap rejection, valid decoder boundaries, StrictMode, timeout and unrelated provider updates remain positive controls.
web_session.limits: Controlled DOM/RPC transport; no physical delivery or rollback guarantee for requests already dispatched. Multi-request body writes remain non-atomic.

rpc_reset_and_stack.contract: Memory-only reset without a devicetree default refuses without deletion; defaults reset in memory; explicit persistent reset can delete. Shared edit staging keeps supported large macro bodies off the RPC stack.
rpc_reset_and_stack.negative_control: Original reset deletes and fails the unchanged refusal assertion. With only reset repaired, the original automatic staging fails the 2048-byte frame guard at MAX_BYTES=2048 after passing ordinary optimized and sanitizer scenarios.
rpc_reset_and_stack.limits: Real handler/nanopb with controlled storage calls; full native owner separately verifies storage/playback. No physical stack high-water or flash-durability measurement.

review_dependency_resolution: Canonical owner resolves actual selected zmk/nanopb west paths. Unset external path variables pass; the original entry fails with missing-path errors.

review_identity_and_authorization.contract: Caller-owned guarded slot-name copies with no truncation, stored body error before success framing, late-lock body encoding refusal, and retired Web calls/drafts/full writes across lock and unlock. Existing fixtures, snapshots, packed admission and full-prefix rewrite controls retained.
review_identity_and_authorization.negative_controls: tests/review_negative_control.py restores borrowed-name, truncate-name, get-admission, encode-lock, web-lock or timer-cleanup only in isolated owner sources; unchanged corresponding assertions must execute and fail.
review_identity_and_authorization.limits: Controlled real registry/kernel/nanopb and DOM boundaries; no physical transport, flash retention or rollback claim. Candidate dependency source must be identified explicitly.

rpc_handler_artifacts.entry: python3 tests/rpc-handler/run.py --output FRESH_ABSOLUTE_OUTPUT; default --variant all is the canonical complete handler matrix
rpc_handler_artifacts.focused: --variant optimized|sanitized|large-body selects one executable; max-name is compile-only acceptance; oversize retains both exact slot/name compiler refusals. Focused output is explicitly not the canonical matrix.
rpc_handler_artifacts.contract: Keep all original compiler flags, C assertions and default counts. Retain generator/generated inputs, selected source/dependency hashes, compiler commands/stdout/stderr, binary/SHA256, actual exit, ordered runtime log and source drift on success or first failure.
rpc_handler_artifacts.repeats: Default executions remain one per executable variant. Fault checks retain the first binary after failure, verify its hash, then execute that same binary in two additional fresh initial-state directories with the recorded environment; three intended C assertion failures required per executable variant.
rpc_handler_artifacts.limits: Artifact/focused controls do not replace complete owner/native/Web checks or establish physical transport. Existing evidence paths are refused.

web_timer_ownership: Frozen lifetime resource with private mutable state; synchronous lock retirement, batched lock/unlock and StrictMode remain covered. Jest runAllTicks drains only fake microtasks before unchanged zero assertions; a real unresolved5s RPC must remain counted1 with no clock advance before retirement. timer-cleanup fault must fail zero-timer assertions.
